title: Dance halls around Elysian Fields and the Hollywood
summary: Third Ward dance halls, the open-air Hollywood owned by Sharkey and Leon Prima, Dave Winstein and Nina Pecone, and Al Rose's book.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Wow. Oh. What about dance halls around Elysian Fields? Do you remember that?

That was, there was, well, you see, there was a lot of people down around that neighborhood. I mean, Uptown was, was a different class of people. It was a, uppity people. But, uh, around that third ward, they, they enjoyed their lives. They enjoyed dancing and things like that. It was, it was more, it was not a society family. They had societies. I mean, uh, what we call, uh, like the different organizations, which were called societies. Uh-huh. But, uh, they were not, uh, the elite. And they used to have these dances on Saturday night.
Which dance halls do you remember?

I don't remember the names of them. Believe me, I don't. Remember the names of the bands down there? Well, that one time they had a band, there was one band down there that was where, on Elysian Fields and, uh, and Saint Bernard, which was the Hollywood. That belonged to Sharkey and Leon Prima. Mm-hmm. That was about, oh no, 35, 40. Yeah. That was a good, open, it was an open air dance hall. Where Schwegman's Grocery Store is now. Down there. And they had, uh, in fact Dave Winstein was working there. In fact the place burned or something like that, I think it burned down. Dave Winstein played there with Nina Pecone and I don't remember. With who? Nina Pecone. Uh-huh. He was a town saxophone player. Nina was very good, very good jazz player, good musician. He's still alive. He used to, he later went to work for, uh, War Lines and they were repairing, repairing saxophones. Reed had some.
and you can see all of that sort of stuff in that book, what's he name wrote? Well you were in a lot of that stuff too.

You talking about Al Rose? Yeah Al Rose. Family album? Yeah. Yeah Edmond Sushant did and he did nearly all of it though. Yeah Edmond Sushant and he did nearly everything. Yeah. They had a little help but mainly they did it all themselves.
